capabilities.name: Publish/Subscribe Messaging
capabilities.notes: Core function of the software. Supports channel subscriptions, multiplexing, and multiple transports.

capabilities.name: Real-time Transport Support
capabilities.notes: Supports WebSocket, HTTP-streaming, SSE, gRPC, and WebTransport.

capabilities.name: Scalability & Persistence
capabilities.notes: Backends supported: Redis (Cluster), PostgreSQL, NATS. Includes async consumers for Kafka/Postgres.

capabilities.name: Message History & Recovery
capabilities.notes: Declared support for hot message history, automatic recovery upon reconnect, and cache recovery mode.

capabilities.name: Authentication & Authorization
capabilities.notes: Supports JWT and proxy-like authentication. Channel permission strategies are mentioned.

dependencies: Redis (or compatible: AWS Elasticache, Valkey, KeyDB, DragonflyDB)
constraints: Requires external backend for scalability/persistence (Redis, PostgreSQL, or NATS) if high availability or history is needed.

assumptions: The component will be deployed as a standalone service.

Integration with the defense architecture's specific MQTT brokers is not direct; Centrifugo uses its own protocol. Adaptation requires building an MQTT-to-Centrifugo bridge or using Centrifugo's HTTP/gRPC API for ingestion.

description: Centrifugo is a scalable, language-agnostic real-time messaging server providing Pub/Sub capabilities over WebSocket, HTTP-streaming, SSE, gRPC, and WebTransport. It acts as a user-facing PUB/SUB server where backends publish via HTTP/gRPC APIs and clients subscribe via SDKs or direct protocol connections. It supports scalability via Redis, PostgreSQL, or NATS backends.
deployment_constraints: Requires external backend for scalability/persistence (Redis, PostgreSQL, or NATS) if high availability or history is needed.
known_gaps: Native MQTT support: Centrifugo does not natively speak MQTT as a transport for clients (it uses WebSocket/SSE/gRPC). The requested 'Position & Telemetry Ingestion (in; MQTT)' and other MQTT interfaces require an external bridge or adapter.

Specific Alert Processing Logic: Centrifugo handles message routing, not business logic like 'Alert Processing' or 'Geofence Violation' detection. These must be implemented in the backend consuming the messages.
risks: Protocol Mismatch: The requested interfaces rely heavily on MQTT. Centrifugo is not an MQTT broker. Using it as a direct replacement for MQTT requires significant architectural adaptation (bridges).
Maintenance: While mature, integrating custom async consumers (Kafka/Postgres) requires Go development effort.

adaptation_assumptions: The component will be deployed as a standalone service.

Integration with the defense architecture's specific MQTT brokers is not direct; Centrifugo uses its own protocol. Adaptation requires building an MQTT-to-Centrifugo bridge or using Centrifugo's HTTP/gRPC API for ingestion.
